newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-REDMAN EARNS FIRST CAREER LPGA VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-REDMAN EARNS FIRST CAREER LPGA VICTORY.

text.p: Michele Redman birdied the final hole to set a tournament record at the $750,000 JAL Big Apple Classic and capture the first LPGA event of her six-year career on Sunday.
Redman, the tournament's first wire-to-wire winner since Juli Inkster in 1992, shot a one-under-par 70 to defeat Annika Sorenstam by three strokes.
Redman's total of 12-under 272 at the 6,176-yard Wykagyl Country Club bettered the tournament record of 273 set by Betsy King in 1990 and equalled by Inkster in 1992 and Tracy Kerdyk in 1995.

The 32-year-old Redman, who took the lead into the final round for the first time in her career, began the day with a four-shot cushion over Sorenstam and Barb Mucha, but bogeyed the first and third holes.
Sorenstam birdied the fifth hole to move within one stroke of Redman, but Redman saved par from the trap and matched Sorenstam over the next four holes for a one-shot lead at the turn.

Sorenstam dropped two strokes back with a bogey on the 10th hole, but Karrie Webb, an Australian who was Rookie of the Year last year, birdied No. 11 to close within one stroke of the lead. However, Redman also birdied the 11th and maintained at least a two-stroke margin the rest of the way to earn $112,500.
Sorenstam shot a 69 to register her fourth runner-up finish of the year at 275. Meg Mallon was alone in third at 276 and Webb and Chris Johnson tied at 277.
